skill.name: grill-me
skill.description: Interviews users with focused questions to stress-test a plan, design, or implementation approach before execution.
skill.summary: Stress-tests plans and designs through structured, one-question-at-a-time interrogation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: No static security findings were reported, and the reviewed prompt-only skill contains no executable code. I found no semantic evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or business-logic abuse.

content.value_statement: Plans often fail because weak assumptions stay hidden. This skill uses direct questioning to expose gaps before work begins.
actual_capabilities: Asks one focused question at a time about a plan or design.
Provides a recommended answer for each question.
Follows dependent decisions through a structured decision tree.
Uses codebase exploration when the answer is available in project files.
Helps identify unclear requirements, risks, and missing tradeoffs.
limitations: It does not execute code or validate runtime behavior.
It depends on the user's answers for business context.
It may be slower than a simple checklist review.
It does not replace expert review for regulated decisions.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Plan
use_cases.description: A product manager can test whether a feature plan has clear goals, constraints, and rollout decisions.

use_cases.title: Challenge a Technical Design
use_cases.description: An engineer can uncover missing edge cases before committing to an architecture or implementation path.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Stakeholder Review
use_cases.description: A team lead can rehearse difficult questions before presenting a project proposal or design decision.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Plan Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you have a simple idea and want early critique.
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill me on this plan. Ask one question at a time and recommend an answer after each question.

prompt_templates.title: Feature Readiness Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before starting a product or engineering task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test this feature proposal. Focus on goals, users, edge cases, dependencies, and launch risks.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Decision Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a technical design has multiple tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Interrogate this architecture decision. Explore each branch of the decision tree and identify unresolved dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Codebase-Aware Planning Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the project files may answer implementation questions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Grill me on this implementation plan. Explore the codebase when it can answer a question more reliably than I can.

output_examples.input: I want to replace our settings page with a new workflow.
output_examples.output: First question: Which user task is currently failing on the settings page? Recommended answer: name one measurable task, not a broad usability goal.

output_examples.input: We plan to migrate billing logic into a shared service.
output_examples.output: First question: Which system owns billing truth during the migration? Recommended answer: choose one owner and define the temporary sync boundary.

output_examples.input: I need to present this launch plan tomorrow.
output_examples.output: First question: What decision do stakeholders need to approve? Recommended answer: separate approval of scope, timeline, and risk acceptance.

best_practices: Start with a concise plan and state the decision you need to make.
Answer each question directly before asking for the next branch.
Share relevant constraints, deadlines, and known risks upfront.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when you only need a quick grammar edit.
Do not skip questions because the recommended answer feels uncomfortable.
Do not treat the output as a final decision without human review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It asks structured questions that expose weak assumptions in a plan or design.

faq.question: Does it answer its own questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a recommended answer with each question to guide the review.

faq.question: Can it inspect a codebase?
faq.answer: Yes, when used in a tool that can read project files and the answer is available there.

faq.question: Is it only for software projects?
faq.answer: No. It can review product, process, and project plans that need structured critique.

faq.question: How should I prepare my prompt?
faq.answer: Describe the plan, the goal, known constraints, and the decision you want to validate.

faq.question: Does it make the final decision?
faq.answer: No. It helps clarify tradeoffs so the user can make a better decision.
